evidence: FUNCTION declarations in REPOSITORY (GnuCOBOL user-defined functions)

purpose.summary: A multi-feature interactive terminal application ('Vault' server) that provides user authentication (login/register), a library/e-book reader, a message board, arcade games (Hangman, Tic-Tac-Toe, random number guessing), a credit/payment system, and an about page. It reads and writes several flat data files for users, books, high scores, game words, and about content.

notable_features: Extensive SCREEN SECTION with FOREGROUND-COLOR, BLINK, UNDERLINE, REVERSE-VIDEO, HIGHLIGHT attributes
REPOSITORY clause declaring multiple user-defined FUNCTION names
UNSIGNED-INT (GnuCOBOL extension) used for index/counter variables
OCCURS ... ASCENDING KEY ... INDEXED BY for sorted in-memory tables (users, books, scores, about)
OCCURS ... DEPENDING ON (ODO) for variable-length message board table
Multiple SELECT/FD pairs for flat LINE SEQUENTIAL files (users, library, high scores, hangman words, about, tic-tac-toe masks)
Pip-Boy ASCII art rendered entirely in SCREEN SECTION VALUE clauses
88-level condition names used extensively for game state (GAME-OVER, WIN-DETECTED, EOF, etc.)
No EXEC SQL, no EXEC CICS, no COMP-3
verdict.notes: Source was truncated to the first 16,000 characters; the PROCEDURE DIVISION is not shown but is confirmed present by mechanical indicators (162 PERFORMs, 6 GOTOs, 15 CALLs). The program is clearly a student/hobbyist project themed around Fallout's Pip-Boy, implementing a text-based multi-menu application in GnuCOBOL with user-defined functions called via REPOSITORY.
